unit.title: Shortest and best: puzzles, paths, packing

lesson.title: Fair turns without clashes
lesson.subtitle: Dots, lines and colours, and turns shared fairly

video.title: Fair turns without clashes
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — your teacher (main character)
Dr Farah Rahman — a visiting teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talks to the student)

scenes.visual: Amina at the board with eight test names and a calendar for the week.
scenes.animation: Test names appear one by one; the calendar flips.
scenes.narration: Test week is coming: eight tests. Some of you take two or three of them, so those tests can’t be at the same time. How few times do we need?

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the Optimization track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: share out times with no clashes, and fair turns for everyone.

scenes.visual: Eight dots in a circle, each labelled with a test; lines appear between some of them.
scenes.animation: Dots pop in; lines draw between them.
scenes.narration: Draw each test as a dot. Join two dots with a line when one pupil takes both tests. A line means: not at the same time!

scenes.visual: The dots fill with colours; joined dots always differ.
scenes.animation: Colours splash onto the dots one by one.
scenes.narration: Now give each dot a colour: each colour is a time. Two dots joined by a line must get different colours. Use as few colours as you can.

scenes.visual: Three dots joined in a triangle: maths, Arabic, French, each a different colour.
scenes.animation: The triangle glows; three colours appear.
scenes.narration: Omar takes maths, Arabic and French. All three are joined to each other, so they need three different times. So three times is the fewest we can use.

scenes.visual: Dr Farah points at the maths dot and the art dot, far apart with no line. Three answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Maths and art are not joined by a line. Can they be at the same time?

scenes.visual: Two colourings side by side: one with four colours, one with three.
scenes.animation: The four-colour plan fades; the three-colour plan glows.
scenes.narration: Yes: no line means no clash. Sharing a time saves a slot. Going down the list in order needs four times, but a clever order needs only three.

scenes.visual: One dot surrounded by many coloured neighbours flashes: it goes next.
scenes.animation: The flashing dot gets its colour; then the next hardest flashes.
scenes.narration: Here’s the clever trick: colour the hardest dot next. That’s the one whose neighbours already use the most colours. Computers plan real exam weeks like this.

scenes.visual: Two pupils’ test calendars: one crammed into a morning, one spread over the week.
scenes.animation: The crammed calendar spreads out over the days.
scenes.narration: Times can be fair or unfair too. If one pupil gets three tests in one morning and another gets one, that’s not fair. A good plan spreads each pupil’s tests out.

scenes.visual: A class rota on the wall with names moving down each day.
scenes.animation: Names shift down one place; a smiley appears.
scenes.narration: It’s the same with turns: who goes first in a game, who cleans the board, who sits by the window. Take turns, so nobody always gets the worst one.

scenes.visual: A phone with the lab: exam dots joined by lines, a finger tapping a dot to change its colour.
scenes.animation: Dots change colour; a red line turns grey when the clash is fixed.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: Exam slots without clashes
scenes.narration: In the app, tap the tests to give them times, with no red lines. Then press Greedy, and DSatur. How few times are really enough?

scenes.visual: Amina points at the triangle of Omar’s three tests. Three answer cards appear.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Omar’s three tests all clash with each other. Can two times be enough for the whole week?

scenes.visual: Summary lines and an orange takeaway bar.
scenes.animation: Lines tick in; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: No: three tests that all clash need three times. Remember: a line means not at the same time. Colour the hardest first. And spread out turns fairly.

scenes.visual: Pupils with coloured pencils drawing dots and lines; a rota chart beside them.
scenes.animation: Colours fill the dots; names appear on the rota.
scenes.narration: Try it at school: draw your class’s clubs or games as dots, and join the ones a friend does both of. Colour them with as few colours as you can. Then make a fair rota for a class job, so everyone takes a turn.

checkpoints.prompt: Maths and art are not joined by a line. Can they be at the same time?

options.text: No: tests can never share a time
Only if they’re in the same room

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — no line means no pupil takes both, so they can share a time.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a line means a clash. With no line, no pupil takes both tests, so they can be at the same time.

checkpoints.prompt: Omar’s three tests all clash with each other. Can two times be enough?

options.text: No: his three tests need three different times
Yes, if he takes them faster

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — three tests that are all joined need three different colours, so at least three times.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — maths, Arabic and French are all joined to each other, so each needs its own time: at least three.
